correctness.rationale: In Z[x]/(x³−x²−1), x⁷=1+2(1+x+2x²), so B mod 2 is 1+x and (B+B²) mod 2 is x+x². Applied to the cyclic parity word (1,1,1,0,1,0,0), their two scalar parity rows are (0,0,1,1,1,0,1) and (0,1,1,1,0,1,0). Writing M^(7·2^r)=I+2^(r+1)D_r, successive squaring gives D_r≡B+B² mod 2 for r≥1; odd multiples preserve the leading term, including r=0. Only classes 2 and 3 pass both rows. Each failing row supplies the counterexample t−s=1 or 2 at s=0. The exact valuation gives finite bijections from t mod 2^(k−1) onto the appropriate parity class mod 2^k, also at k=1. The seven-letter nonconstant parity period forces any period to be a multiple of seven, and the difference law at j=2 forces the stated dyadic factor. Completing the compatible quotient bijections gives the asserted 2-adic isometries.
residual_risks: The proof certifies the two sections, not the full multiplicity of every scalar residue across all seven classes.
